hook.text: The quintet recorded it over three days in September 2007 at Capitol Studios in Los Angeles.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: 19 to 21 September 2007, Capitol Studios, Los Angeles

sentences.text: The album was a return to hard bop for Roy Hargrove, a style he had long been drawn to.
Before it, he had made several albums that explored jazz within hip-hop and R&B.
Hargrove wrote seven of the thirteen tracks, and the rest come from other writers, Sam Cooke among them.
Roy Hargrove and Larry Clothier produced the record, with Jacques Muyal as executive producer.
Al Schmitt recorded and mixed it, and Steve Genewick was the engineer.
Hargrove played trumpet and flugelhorn, Justin Robinson played alto saxophone and flute, and Gerald Clayton played piano.
Danton Boller played bass and Montez Coleman played drums, five players in all.

listen_for.text: Cedar Walton wrote it, and it opens the record.
Kurt Weill and Ogden Nash wrote it, so it is one of the tunes on the record that Hargrove did not write.

listen_for.track: Bring It On Home To Me
listen_for.text: Sam Cooke wrote it, and it closes the record.
